idea-plugin.name: Try/Catch Consistency Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Learns the dominant checked-exception-handling convention YOUR OWN FILE already established for a given method -- not a rule this plugin knew in advance -- and flags a gutter warning on the call sites that break with it. If 8 or more calls to the same method in a file all catch the same checked exception (or all deliberately let it propagate uncaught), and one new call site disagrees, that is a real, concrete signal something was missed -- without the plugin needing to know anything about the method, the framework, or the exception type in advance.

A convention learned from your own code, not a pre-written rule -- this is fundamentally different from every other plugin in this catalog: instead of shipping a fixed pattern to detect, it builds a per-file statistical consensus (via real PSI: resolveMethod(), throws-list resolution, try/ catch ancestor walking) and flags the minority that contradicts the majority it just observed. No Marketplace plugin found doing this kind of self-referential, learned- from-the-codebase consistency check.

Stated honestly: v0.1 is bounded to the current file only (comparing against every call site in the whole project would require an unbounded-cost project-wide search on every background highlight pass) and to checked exceptions only (unchecked/RuntimeException handling is never required by the compiler, so "inconsistent" carries much weaker signal there). Requires at least 8 calls to the same method in one file before it says anything -- small files never trigger a false "convention".

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
